Warren Buffett donates $5.47 billion in Berkshire shares to four charities, backs successor Greg Abel
stories.summary: Warren Buffett has donated approximately $5.47 billion worth of Berkshire Hathaway shares to four charitable foundations associated with his three children. The 96-year-old billionaire also reiterated his confidence in successor Greg Abel, saying his faith in Berkshire Hathaway's new leadership remains as strong as ever. The donation takes his total charitable contributions beyond $29 billion.

stories.title: Warren Buffett donates $5.47 billion more, taking family charity gifts past $29 billion
stories.summary: Warren Buffett has ramped up his charitable efforts, revealing a staggering donation of Berkshire Hathaway shares valued at $5.47 billion. This sizable contribution focuses primarily on four family-operated charities, with a significant portion directed to the Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation. With an earlier donation nearing $6 billion, his total charitable giving surpasses $11.4 billion in 2026.

stories.title: Martine Moise enters Haiti's first presidential election in a decade
stories.summary: Martine Moise has officially entered the race for Haiti's upcoming presidential election set for July next year, marking a significant moment as it will be the first election in almost a decade. Amidst ongoing security concerns and political turmoil, Moise's candidacy is particularly poignant given her ties to recent events. With 33 candidates on the ballot, Haitian voters will face critical choices that could reshape the country's political future.

stories.title: 'I may not return alive': Ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan seeks urgent medical help
stories.summary: Imran Khan has appealed to Pakistan's top courts for urgent medical care for himself and his wife. He claims that his health has deteriorated significantly during solitary confinement, where he is held for up to 22 hours daily. Khan alleges that authorities neglected previous court orders regarding his medical treatment and communication with family. He expressed concern for his wife's rapidly declining vision and health after a recent surgery.

stories.title: Canadian teacher's death inspires charity that has donated more than $5 million to children over 13 years
stories.summary: A Canadian charity named Noelle's Gift to Children has reached a significant milestone by distributing $5 million. In the past year, the charity provided $259,200 in funding to two school boards. This funding assists students with essential items such as food, clothing, and healthcare needs. The charity originated in 2013 after a kindergarten teacher's tragic death.

stories.title: Brazilian Uber driver was stabbed 10 times and left quadriplegic but she doesn't want to leave the country. She begs Australia to let her stay after her student visa expires during hospitalization
Census 2027: Self-enumeration begins in four states, house-to-house count from December 1
stories.summary: The Census 2027 self-enumeration process has commenced in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Goa, and Uttarakhand, running until November 30. Following this, house-to-house enumeration will begin on December 1. The initiative aims to gather a range of data, including caste details from respondents, with an open-ended approach. Meanwhile, Manipur's census has been postponed due to local concerns regarding the national register of citizens.

stories.title: IISc researchers find antibiotic combination to reverse drug resistance in TB
'I felt accepted': Sonia Gandhi revisits 2004 Cong win, opens up at memoir launch
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi's memoir release shed light on her journey of acceptance in India post the 2004 Congress victory. She shared her early experiences with Indira Gandhi, detailing feelings of both intimidation and admiration over time. Following the tragic assassination of Rajiv Gandhi, her children emerged as pillars of emotional strength. Sonia's message to the youth emphasizes the importance of participating in politics and civic life.

stories.title: H-E-B surprises 10,000 Texas shoppers with $100 gift cards worth $1 million
stories.summary: On November 14, H-E-B surprised customers by distributing $1 million worth of gift cards, providing a significant boost to 10,000 shoppers during grocery checkout. This generous giveaway of $100 gift cards aims to alleviate the financial strain many face as the holidays approach. H-E-B's initiative underscores their dedication to uplifting Texas communities, showcasing how thoughtful gestures can have a meaningful impact in tough economic times.

stories.title: Jake Gyllenhaal joins celebrity auction supporting homes for injured veterans
stories.summary: Jake Gyllenhaal is joining the 10th annual Veterans Day Celebrity Auction, presented by Homes For Our Troops. This auction provides fans a unique opportunity to bid on exclusive experiences and memorabilia while supporting injured veterans. Bidding is open from November 10 until November 20, 2026, with proceeds aiding the construction of adapted, mortgage-free homes for veterans with serious injuries.

stories.title: A decade out of power: Why Congress is struggling to make a comeback in Uttarakhand

Massachusetts cinema gets another $10 million gift, bringing $23 million restoration closer to reality
stories.summary: West Newton Cinema is nearing the end of its restoration effort, thanks to a generous $10 million donation. This funding aims to improve accessibility and bolster ongoing construction. A cherished part of the community, the cinema features a diverse array of films and events. Looking ahead, future renovations will refresh seating and the exterior, with hopes of gathering the final funding through community contributions.

stories.title: New York woman fights neighbours over ownership of land strip she maintained for 29 years
stories.summary: Lauren Sullivan, a resident of New York, has initiated a legal battle over a slender strip of land she maintains between her home and her neighbors'. Having cared for this space for almost three decades, Sullivan's lawsuit proceeds after the court denied a dismissal request. Her neighbors, Lisa and John Walts, challenge her claim, stating her long-term maintenance isn't sufficient under the law.

stories.title: Minneapolis landlord owes more than $1 million in unpaid utility bills as tenants raise concerns over building conditions
stories.summary: Residents at several properties in Minneapolis, managed by Fine Associates, are facing ongoing maintenance problems that remain unaddressed. They are questioning the allocation of their rent, particularly regarding unpaid utility charges. The city is now transferring these delinquent accounts to Hennepin County for recovery via property taxes. In response, tenants are organizing unions and exploring legal options, expressing their deep need for essential maintenance amidst growing frustration.

stories.title: Intimidatory speech case: Abhishek Banerjee seeks extension of protection; Calcutta HC to hear plea on Nov 20
Poland detains three teens over 'terror plot' linked to neo-Nazi movement
stories.summary: Poland has seen the arrest of three teenagers connected to neo-Nazi factions, facing serious allegations of planning terrorist acts. Their activities caught the attention of the internal security agency, which found them discussing the creation of homemade bombs and firearms using messaging platforms. One of the suspects was discovered with chemical materials ideal for explosives, prompting significant legal charges.

stories.title: 570 Rocky lookalikes set Guinness World Record at Philadelphia Museum steps 50 years after film
stories.summary: On November 13, 570 fans dressed in grey tracksuits gathered at the Philadelphia Museum of Art to set a record. Participants included individuals from across the globe, including countries like Germany and Hungary. The event celebrated 50 years since the iconic film Rocky was released, highlighting its cultural significance. After the record announcement, attendees enjoyed running up the museum steps while chanting Rocky's name.

stories.title: '520 drains discharge wastewater in the Yamuna': SC raps admin over rising pollution despite huge spending

'No one excluded': CM Yogi Adityanath says Census 2027 will ensure welfare benefits for all
stories.summary: In a significant move for Census 2027, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has initiated the self-enumeration process in Lucknow. Emphasizing the importance of precise data for identifying individuals missing from welfare initiatives, he outlined how this census will collect vital demographic details to inform the development of crucial infrastructure such as health centers and schools.

stories.title: 'Dalit oppression, land grab': BJP hits back at Akhilesh over 'Damdar Dalit' remarks
stories.summary: In response to Akhilesh Yadav's recent appeal to the Dalit community, BJP leaders have launched a series of critiques against the Samajwadi Party chief. They pointed out the SP's past failures regarding Dalit issues during its tenure, with Uttar Pradesh MSME minister Bhupendra Singh Chaudhary highlighting various incidents of Dalit oppression.

stories.title: Ajit Pawar plane crash: Maharashtra CM urges Amit Shah to fast-track probe, release early report
Union minister Suresh Gopi says diesel, price cuts 'not possible right away'; cites Rs 42,000 crore losses
stories.summary: Union Minister Suresh Gopi highlighted the challenges posed by Rs 42,000 crore losses in the oil sector, stating that lowering fuel prices is currently impractical. While consumers are eager for cuts, he noted that immediate adjustments are not feasible. Furthermore, he encouraged state governments to ease tax burdens on petrol.

stories.title: 'Who ordered SIR?' Congress seeks SC nod to pose 48 questions to EC, CEC Gyanesh Kumar over 'vote chori'
stories.summary: In a significant move, Congress has voiced its apprehensions over the Election Commission of India's affidavit to the Supreme Court. They emphasize that their pressing inquiries into purported electoral roll irregularities remain largely unaddressed. The party has compiled a list of 48 detailed questions for the Election Commission, focusing on aspects such as the Special Intensive Revision process.

stories.title: Parents fled Mozambique with unregistered newborn; 26 yrs later, Gujarat woman gets Indian passport
stories.summary: Dolly Vadalia, originally from Mozambique, encountered significant obstacles in her quest for Indian citizenship due to a lack of documentation. After her marriage in 2023, multiple attempts to secure her passport were denied due to her parents' failure to register her birth. However, the Indian embassy stepped in to ensure her birth was recorded, and on November 11, she finally obtained her Indian passport.

stories.title: 'When CM was unavailable, Ajit Pawar was there': Amit Shah remembers ex-Maharashtra deputy CM
stories.summary: During a significant bust unveiling event, Amit Shah shared heartfelt condolences on the untimely passing of Ajit Pawar. He acknowledged Pawar’s impactful contributions, especially during the challenging Covid-19 pandemic, contrasting his proactive approach with prior government communication challenges. Meanwhile, Maharashtra’s Chief Minister, Devendra Fadnavis, urgently called for the swift release of the investigation report into the tragic plane crash that took Ajit Pawar's life on January 28.

'Hand of unity' vs 'unhinged incitement': Likud, Eisenkot trade barbs over Netanyahu's offer
Ohio man, 78, visits all 50 US state fairs in retirement, with 19 still to go
stories.summary: At the age of 75, Jim Chew was ready for new adventures after retirement. With 31 state fairs already visited, he set a goal to explore all 50 by 2030. Each fair offers him a taste of local culture, foods, and a chance to connect with diverse communities. Jim's organized excursions aim to enrich his journey across the nation, filling his days with exciting experiences instead of monotony.

stories.title: After 100 years of extinction, baby oysters found in Scottish estuary; 140,000 adults returned over 12 years
stories.summary: After more than 100 years, scientists found young European flat oysters in Dornoch Firth, indicating successful natural breeding and conservation. The project aimed to restore native oyster populations through the introduction of adult oysters, totaling around 140,000, over 12 years. Restoration efforts have shown progress as oysters are now reproducing naturally in their habitat. The project supports marine biodiversity by enhancing ecosystems through oyster reef formation.

stories.title: Over 28 cyclists carry Thanksgiving turkeys on their bikes in Maine; unusual ride helps 58 families get free holiday dinners
stories.summary: More than 28 cyclists participated in the eighth annual Turkey Ride to deliver Thanksgiving turkeys. They gathered at Maine Sport Rockport and picked up items from Hannaford Supermarkets. After collecting donations, they transported the groceries to the Camden Area Christian Food Pantry. Fifty-eight families benefited from the food pantry's effort, receiving turkeys for their Thanksgiving meals. The event highlighted community support for those in need and encouraged charitable involvement.

stories.title: At 102, WWII veteran who helped liberate Dachau receives France’s Legion of Honor; still drives and lives independently
stories.summary: At 102 years old, William Lyford received France's prestigious Legion of Honor, honoring his bravery during World War II, particularly his role in liberating Dachau concentration camp in 1945. The touching ceremony held in Woodstock was filled with family, friends, and fellow veterans celebrating his significant contributions. Despite his service, Lyford’s daughter shared how he rarely discussed his military past, showcasing the lasting bond between the U.S. and France.

stories.title: 103-year-old D-Day veteran receives replacement medals 80 years after returning his uniform
stories.summary: Douglas Halley, a 103-year-old D-Day veteran, recently received his wartime medals which were lost in 1945. A young historian, Joseph Smith, discovered Halley's military record while researching veterans' stories and assisted in recovering the medals. The Ministry of Defence located and mailed the medals back to Halley just before Remembrance Day. This story highlights the importance of remembering personal histories and the sacrifices of war.

stories.title: Man finds centuries-old gold ring after 15 minutes of metal detecting
stories.summary: Kevin Short found a centuries-old gold ring inscribed “I live in hope” just 15 minutes into a metal-detecting search in Warwickshire. Authenticated by the British Museum, the 16th-to-18th-century ring is expected to fetch up to £3,000 at a December 2 auction.

stories.title: Australian reptile park welcomes first king cobra hatchlings in 16 years
'Insult to faith': BJP shares video of Congress leader Devendra Yadav throwing plastic bottle in Yamuna
stories.summary: BJP condemned Congress party leader Devendra Yadav for allegedly polluting the Yamuna River during Chhath Puja. The BJP accused Congress of disrespecting the faith of Chhath devotees amidst environmental concerns. Cleaning efforts are underway as pollution in the Yamuna raises public health issues ahead of the festival. Authorities are preparing designated ghats for devotees while addressing river pollution.

stories.title: ‘Does Bengal belong to Bengalis or rogue Biharis?’ TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee's remarks on Chhath spark row
stories.summary: A political controversy has emerged in West Bengal over Chhath Puja preparations, led by TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee's statements. Banerjee alleged that the state was being dominated by non-Bengalis and accused the BJP government of neglecting Bengali culture. West Bengal minister Indranil Khan and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari defended the arrangements for Chhath Puja and rejected claims of cultural appropriation.

stories.title: 'Not AI, this is Yamuna': AAP, BJP lock horns over Chhath celebrations in Delhi 'amid toxic foam'
stories.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) accused the BJP governments in Delhi and at the Centre of making false claims about cleaning the Yamuna as Purvanchali devotees celebrated Chhath Puja at its ghats. Citing toxic foam in the river, AAP targeted Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, while the BJP defended its clean-up efforts and hit back at the previous AAP government.

stories.title: 'Inappropriate to lecture India on democracy': Meloni ally hits back at Italian leader's BJP vote theft jibe
stories.summary: Deborah Bergamini has expressed discontent over Giacomo Filibeck's remarks on India’s electoral process. She emphasized that India has its own political institutions to handle such disputes. Filibeck’s comments occurred during the Bharat Summit 2026, where he supported the Indian Congress Party. The BJP responded by accusing the Congress of seeking foreign interference in national matters. This situation highlights ongoing tensions between Indian political factions regarding electoral integrity and foreign influence.

stories.title: 3 grenades found in polythene bag defused in J&K's Baramulla
stories.summary: Security forces defused three grenades found in a polythene bag in north Kashmir's Baramulla district, as news agency ANI reported Monday. The recovery comes days after police arrested a man and seized two hand grenades from a forest in Tangmarg. Police are investigating the source of the explosives, their intended use and possible links.

stories.title: BJP MP Ajeet Gopchade urges PM Modi to ensure representation of divyang persons in Parliament
stories.summary: Ajeet Gopchade has requested Prime Minister Narendra Modi to develop mechanisms for the representation of divyang persons. He highlighted the successful examples from other countries that facilitate this representation in legislatures. Gopchade suggested that exceptional candidates with disabilities should be considered for Rajya Sabha nominations. The Prime Minister's Office has forwarded his suggestions to relevant ministries for further action.

stories.title: 'Perfectly safe' but not 'maxed out'? Trump takes Qatar jet to Asia
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to travel to Asia on Monday aboard the aircraft gifted by Qatar, even as questions remain over its promised security upgrades. According to NBC News, the jet has received some maintenance and cosmetic improvements, but the larger overhaul remains unclear months after an Iran-related security scare forced Trump to fly home from Turkey on a secret military plane.

Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites as ULA's Vulcan rocket fails minutes after launch
stories.summary: Amazon's planned launch of 40 satellites for its Leo internet network failed after the Vulcan rocket malfunctioned. The Vulcan rocket, operated by United Launch Alliance, experienced an anomaly 10 minutes after liftoff. This failure poses a setback for Amazon's satellite internet plans, which aim to compete with Elon Musk's Starlink. Amazon has also invested in other launch options including Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket and Arianespace.

stories.title: 'Not Cuba or Venezuela': Iran warns it will not wait for US attack before responding
stories.summary: Iran has expressed that it is ready for potential military action while discussing diplomatic avenues with the United States. Deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi indicated three possible scenarios: diplomatic talks, economic blockades, and military response. Tehran has set specific conditions, including ending the war and lifting economic sanctions for any agreement. The arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East adds to ongoing regional tensions.

stories.title: Colorado jury awards $65 million, after mother killed in crash
stories.summary: A jury in Colorado awarded $65 million to the family of Megan Arneson, who was killed in 2022. Arneson died when a truck carrying an improperly loaded excavator struck an I-25 overpass. Her 10-year-old son, who was in the vehicle, witnessed the tragic incident. The truck driver and the company both bore responsibility for the accident in the court's findings.

stories.title: Palm Beach estate tied to foreclosure suit asks $32 million
stories.summary: A mansion located at 301 Plantation Road in Palm Beach is currently listed for sale at $32 million. The property has a history of foreclosure proceedings after the seller defaulted on a $22 million mortgage. This brand-new estate features over 9,000 square feet, seven bedrooms, and luxurious amenities like a double infinity-edge pool. A total of 21 luxury deals were signed in Palm Beach County during a recent week.

stories.title: Noose tightens on Bishnoi: Cops seek jail visitor logs, up security for B-town stars
Ray of hope has reached Gadchiroli this Diwali: PM
Those using Form 6 to re-enroll won't be prosecuted: EC to SC
stories.summary: The Election Commission has committed to include every eligible citizen in the electoral rolls during the current process. No legal action will be taken against individuals for re-registering to vote through Form 6. Voters are advised to ensure their names are not listed in other constituencies before applying. Additionally, those previously removed erroneously can submit fresh forms for their names to be reinstated.

stories.title: 'No case against me anywhere,' Lalit Modi claims to TOI
stories.summary: IPL founder Lalit Modi, who left India in 2010 amid allegations of tax evasion, money laundering and proxy ownership linked to IPL, has announced he has received British citizenship. Lalit was appearing at an event at Oxford Union when he made the announcement.

stories.title: Alabama mother regains parental rights to older child; court upholds termination for younger child
stories.summary: A recent ruling by an Alabama appeals court has partially overturned a juvenile court's ruling regarding parental rights. The mother has maintained her rights to her older child but lost her rights to her younger daughter. The court underscored the necessity of evaluating the circumstances of each child individually in such matters. Meanwhile, the father's rights to both children remain revoked due to evidence of substance abuse and inadequate support.

stories.title: Lalit gets British citizenship, extradition prospects take a hit
stories.summary: Lalit Modi has announced his acquisition of British citizenship during an event at Oxford Union. While he claims to have faced threats and political persecution, he has refused to return to India. The Enforcement Directorate has ongoing investigations regarding his alleged financial misconduct linked to IPL. Previous requests for his deportation have been denied by the UK government.

stories.title: San Francisco 'Painted Lady' bought for $1.85 million now listed for $5.595 million
stories.summary: Once a forgotten Victorian gem in Noe Valley, this home was purchased at $1.85 million and thoughtfully revived, blending its charming historic features with modern amenities. Now boasting a listing price of $5.595 million, it offers five spacious bedrooms alongside a private apartment. The extensive restoration preserved its Victorian allure while ensuring necessary structural and aesthetic updates, reflecting the growing trend of revitalizing historic homes in sought-after urban areas.

stories.title: Empty Vande Bharat allowed to run 463km despite 'poor power brake'
stories.summary: An empty Vande Bharat train journeyed 463 kilometers from Hatia to Deen Dayal Upadhyaya station despite brake problems. Two loco pilots had reported issues with the power brake before the journey commenced. An investigation revealed that brakes on every coach had been isolated, leading to joint brake failure. The South Eastern Railway's document indicated staff negligence in integrating the braking systems.

stories.title: Criminal killed in 5th 'encounter' in West Bengal since May
CRPF men in anti-Naxal ops diverted to Manipur
Shah hits back at Rahul, says he's defaming India at global platforms
Alabama court upholds mother's sole custody after harassment, but orders new visitation schedule
stories.summary: After sending threatening emails to his ex-wife, an Alabama father grappled with custody issues. The court granted sole custody to the mother, citing the father's harassment. Although the appeals court upheld this decision, they recognized that the father's visitation hours were excessively limited. Consequently, a reassessment of the visitation schedule was ordered, while a protection order against him remains active until March 2027.

stories.title: Alabama student Jai Varikuti's UNICEF campaign raises nearly $5,500 across six schools
Georgia woman wins $2.5m after rear-end crash leads to spinal fusion surgery
stories.summary: A woman from Georgia received a substantial $2.5 million settlement for severe neck injuries resulting from a car accident in 2023. The incident occurred when her vehicle was rear-ended while awaiting at a traffic light. Following the crash, she underwent significant medical interventions, including spinal surgery. Her legal team emphasized how these injuries drastically altered her quality of life, highlighting the profound consequences of personal injuries.

stories.title: India bucks trend, 38 institutions up in QS sustainability study
Govt healthcare spend up 3x since 2013-14 to 4.1L cr
stories.summary: Out-Of-Pocket Expense Dips But Families Still Paid 4L Cr In 2023-24

stories.title: 'Don't make me go with him': Pennsylvania father barred from contacting son, ex-partner for 3 years
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania appeals court has upheld a three-year protection order barring a father from contacting his former partner and their seven-year-old son. The mother alleged that he pushed his way into her home during a custody handoff, behaved aggressively and frightened the child, who later begged her not to send him with his father again.

stories.title: George’s Drawing Published: Prince George’s kingfisher art appears; links three generations
stories.summary: In an exclusive edition of Country Life magazine, Prince George displayed his artistic skills with a thoughtful drawing of a kingfisher. This special issue, guided by his father Prince William, emphasizes issues such as environmental awareness and family life. Through this public piece, George connects to the creative spirit of his mother, Kate Middleton, and his grandfather, King Charles III, promoting the royal family's dedication to nature and social engagement.

stories.title: Venezuelan doctor honoured after saving toddler from drowning in Georgia pool
stories.summary: Dr. Andrea Sansonnet saved one-year-old Maddox from drowning at a swimming pool in Newnan, Georgia. Her quick actions included performing CPR until he was breathing again after being underwater for about 90 seconds. On their shared birthday, the Newnan Police Department honored Dr. Sansonnet for her lifesaving efforts during the emergency. Maddox’s mother expressed gratitude for the doctor’s presence when the incident occurred.

stories.title: California mother and newborn died after discharge; jury awards $9.25m, but old law limits payout
stories.summary: Demi Dominguez tragically lost her life shortly after hospital discharge, following alarming preeclampsia symptoms. Her baby son, Malakhi De Leon, passed away soon after birth. A jury subsequently awarded $9.25 million in damages, yet limitations under California's MICRA restrict non-economic compensation. This heart-wrenching case underscores the urgent necessity for reform in medical negligence laws, as the families advocate for changes to protect others from similar tragedies.

stories.title: 12-year study finds declining elephant numbers lead to fragmented social networks
stories.summary: A study in Udawalawe National Park indicates that dwindling elephant groups result in significant social vulnerabilities. With fewer individuals, elephants transition from larger communities to smaller, more isolated factions, which impairs their capacity to nurture and feed effectively. Once a critical social threshold is exceeded, the difficulty of reversing such fragmentation intensifies.

stories.title: Charleston opens $25m memorial 11 years after church shooting killed nine Black worshippers
stories.summary: In Charleston, South Carolina, the Emanuel Nine Memorial has been unveiled, marking over a decade since the heart-wrenching shooting. Families and community figures participated in the dedication ceremony, honoring those lost in the tragic event. The memorial features peaceful benches and a beautiful fountain, designed for contemplation and remembrance. Chris Singleton emphasized its personal importance in honoring his mother's legacy.

stories.title: Congress suggests Army ‘friendly fire’ behind deaths of 2 SPOs, BJP calls it 'provocative'
stories.summary: In Jammu and Kashmir, Congress has called for a thorough investigation into the tragic killing of two special police officers. Initial reports indicate that the officers may have been accidentally shot by Army personnel during a hunting operation. The BJP has dismissed these allegations, claiming they tarnish the integrity of the security forces.

stories.title: Mumbai physics forum hosts online lecture by Pak N-scientist
stories.summary: Mumbai recently held an online event to honor the birth centenary of Nobel laureate Abdus Salam. Eminent scientist Pervez Amirali Hoodbhoy delivered a lecture discussing Salam's contributions to physics and his life. Hoodbhoy highlighted Salam's significance as a symbol of goodwill between India and Pakistan. He mentioned Salam's lack of recognition in Pakistan due to his Ahmadiyya sect affiliation, affecting youth role models.

stories.title: Kashmir film fraternity trains guns on Bollywood’s ‘AK-47 & skullcap’ stereotype, seeks own industry
stories.summary: Kashmiri filmmakers are advocating for a shift towards regional cinema to enhance authentic storytelling and representation. They argue that Bollywood often reinforces stereotypes that misrepresent life in J&K. The current film policy is criticized for not adequately supporting local productions while favoring external filmmakers. Actors and directors are calling for collaboration among regional artists to develop a unique Kashmiri film industry, signaling a significant movement towards self-identity and cultural expression.

stories.title: Pennsylvania court rejects son's claim of missing millions from 65-property family trust
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania court has upheld the dismissal of Jacob Singer's case over alleged mismanagement of a family trust holding around 65 properties. It found that his claim of missing millions lacked sufficient financial evidence and that he had not established a right to an accounting or immediate control of the properties.

stories.title: Minting Accident: 3D tests suggest sixpence was deformed during minting; cause remains inconclusive
stories.summary: A team of researchers has thoroughly examined a distorted silver sixpence from 1834, uncovering unexpected manufacturing flaws. Through intricate 3D imaging, they revealed significant deformations and patterns that stray from regular wear. This peculiar state of the coin prompts a deeper look into the production methods of the steam-powered minting period. The analysis, combining advanced imaging and chemistry, sheds light on historical minting defects.

stories.title: An Australian railway enthusiast spent 13 years building a mini version of a 315-kilometre route
stories.summary: After 13 years of meticulous work, Peter Michalak has crafted a stunning miniature railway that faithfully mirrors the Adelaide-to-Bridgewater route. This impressive model showcases various stations across a detailed 315-kilometre stretch. Initially designed to be portable, the project has since transitioned into a permanent display rich in detail, reflecting Michalak's family history and personal ties to the railway. Efforts are ongoing to enhance this intricate layout over the next decade.

stories.title: Kishtwar BJP leader questions Shagun Parihar’s mosque claim, Muslim body seeks public apology
Humane World for Animals rescues 951 chinchillas from Ohio breeding facility in two operations
stories.summary: A breeding facility in Jenera, Ohio, was revealed to have hundreds of chinchillas in poor conditions. Federal inspections led to the discovery of severe neglect and health issues in the animals. Humane World for Animals assisted in the rescue of 951 chinchillas, which were removed in two operations. The facility's owner agreed to surrender the animals and cease operations regulated by the Animal Welfare Act.

stories.title: Launching new anti-anaemia strategy without enough evidence could waste public funds, warn experts
Punjab BJP forms manifesto, 'chargesheet' committees; Raghav Chadha, Harbhajan Singh among members
stories.summary: Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon has created two vital committees. One will meticulously draft the party manifesto, while the other focuses on compiling a detailed chargesheet. Senior leaders Avinash Rai Khanna and Sunil Jakhar are at the helm, supported by a diverse range of experts, showcasing the party's commitment to thorough preparation for a strategic electoral campaign.

stories.title: South Dakota ranchers report wildlife boom after adopting satellite-guided rotational grazing
stories.summary: In South Dakota, a ranching family has harnessed the power of rotational grazing and cutting-edge virtual fencing to rejuvenate their land's biodiversity. By allowing grasslands to rest between grazing sessions, they have significantly improved plant health and restored native ecology. This approach not only boosts wildlife populations, such as diverse bird species and larger mammals, but also streamlines cattle management with reduced labor.

stories.title: 'Well-planned conspiracy': BJP refutes reports of 209-candidate list for upcoming UP elections
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party's Uttar Pradesh unit has refuted claims regarding a supposed list of 209 candidates. Officials described these reports as false and part of a larger scheme. They cautioned party members against believing in unverified media stories. Additionally, they clarified that the assembly election candidate selection process has yet to commence, highlighting the importance of a methodical and unified approach to such decisions.

stories.title: Prince William, Kate to meet PM Modi in Delhi during three-day India visit
'Divide-and-rule tactics': RSS chief Bhagwat's warning over attempts to split India
stories.summary: During a recent event in Jodhpur, RSS leader Mohan Bhagwat spoke fervently about the necessity of national unity. He indicated that smaller identities can lead to societal rifts, reminiscent of colonial tactics. Emphasizing the need for individuals to set aside ego and self-interest, he illustrated his points with lessons from the Mahabharata, stressing that unity is key to overcoming challenges.

stories.title: Utah couple turns pandemic candy search into business stocked in more than 500 US stores
Kishtwar SPOs killings: BJP says Congress remarks could fuel Pakistan propaganda, seeks apology
'Won't disappoint my workers': Kumaraswamy says he will decide on Karnataka return at right time
Arunachal governor reviews security in 3 districts, pushes for faster Myanmar border fencing
stories.summary: Governor KT Parnaik held a review meeting to assess the security dynamics in Tirap, Changlang, and Longding districts. He emphasized the urgency of advancing the border fencing initiative along the Myanmar border and called for decisive steps against drug trafficking. Highlighting the importance of collaboration among security forces and local administration, the governor voiced his worries over the delays in the fencing project and the increasing drug-related cross-border issues.

stories.title: Supertanker with 2 million barrels of oil sinks after hitting mine in Strait of Hormuz
Trump slams judge’s order blocking Washington golf course renovation
Nevada rancher permanently protects 1,228 acres for sage-grouse habitat and farming
stories.summary: David Park has successfully conserved 1,228 acres of land at Desert Creek Ranch in Nevada. This effort focuses on protecting habitats for the rare Bi-State sage-grouse while allowing continued agricultural activities. A permanent conservation agreement prevents non-agricultural development and preserves the land's ecological value. Additionally, a future grant will facilitate restoration work across 350 acres to control invasive grass and support biodiversity.

stories.title: 'No place for goons': CM Adhikari's warning to criminals after encounter of Shantiniketan accused
stories.summary: In a bold statement, Suvendu Adhikari, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, sent a clear message to those involved in crime after a police encounter resulted in the death of Ratan Sheikh, a prime suspect who reportedly shot at officers during his attempted arrest. Adhikari reaffirmed that criminal activities will not be tolerated in the state. Meanwhile, the police constable injured in the incident remains in stable condition.

stories.title: Texas family's rescued bluebonnet painting sells for $112,500 at auction
Kulgam terror attack: Search operation launched in J&K to hunt terrorists who attacked CRPF post
After 46 years, Oklahoma food bank serves its billionth meal; Thunder adds $25,000 donation
stories.summary: On November 10, the Regional Food Bank of Oklahoma marked a historic milestone by packaging its one billionth meal, a testament to 46 years of tireless support from community partners and volunteers. The Oklahoma City Thunder made a significant donation to amplify hunger relief efforts. However, food insecurity still poses a critical challenge in Oklahoma, particularly affecting children.

stories.title: US State Secretary Marco Rubio blames Iran’s ‘expansionist mentality’ for conflicts across Middle East
Punjab polls: Sukhbir Badal to take final call on alliance, says SAD leader
TMC vs TMC: Mamata-led faction submits affidavits to EC, accuses rival group of forgery
Historic Virginia school for Black children reopens as museum after $6.2m restoration
stories.summary: The historic Union Street School in Leesburg, Virginia has reopened as a museum and community centre. After a refurbishment costing around $6.2 million, the building now serves to educate about Black history. Initially established in 1884, it provided education to Black children during segregation until 1958. The new museum aims to preserve memories and share the stories of those associated with the school.

stories.title: Beavers reintroduced to an English estate changed its stream within a year
stories.summary: The Spains Hall Estate in Essex has welcomed the return of beavers, leading to remarkable improvements in the local ecosystem. A year after their reintroduction, studies revealed an increase in both the quantity and diversity of terrestrial invertebrates. Additionally, water quality enhancements were noted, with elevated oxygen levels and diminished nitrate concentrations.

stories.title: Archaeologists digging in Beijing have found the first Great Wall remains from the Sui dynasty
stories.summary: Recent archaeological discoveries in Beijing have unearthed remnants of the Great Wall from the Sui Dynasty, revolutionizing our understanding of its historical context. This find emphasizes the wall's role as a military outpost on the northern frontier. Additionally, three ancient wooden boats, dating back approximately 1,800 years, were recovered in Fengtai district, showcasing an early transport network in Beijing and shedding light on the area's trade and defense roles.

stories.title: Kentucky man says agent sold him his own home and pressured him for an extra $85,000
stories.summary: After hiring estate agent Rick Walters to sell his home, Jason Wagner later bought a property from him. Wagner alleges he was coerced into paying an extra $85,000 above their original agreement. The Kentucky Court of Appeals reinstated many of Wagner's claims against Walters and Lenihan Real Estate, allowing him to proceed in a lower court after previous dismissals. The decision emphasized concerns regarding Walters' financial transactions during the sale.

stories.title: 'Very grim picture': Gauhati HC flags 1.16 lakh declared foreigners yet to be apprehended in Assam
NYPD shoots kidnapping suspect dead after van chase on busy highway; no child found
'Who laughs when India is insulted?' Rijiju takes digs at Rahul Gandhi over foreign leader's remarks on democracy
Akhilesh calls Dalits 'damdar', vows to wipe out BJP in UP
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav emphasized the importance of the Dalit community in upcoming Uttar Pradesh elections. He called for the ousting of the BJP government, highlighting the need for social justice. Akhilesh criticized the ruling party's record on Dalit issues, which includes the vandalism of Dr. BR Ambedkar's statues. He promised that a Samajwadi Party government would prioritize rights and education for marginalized communities.

stories.title: From Sonia-Natwar row to Advani's Jinnah remarks: 5 political memoirs that stirred storm
Missouri appeals court voids $1 million in punitive damages against therapist in affair case
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, the Missouri Court of Appeals reinforced a jury's verdict against therapist Craig Politte for professional misconduct, confirming charges of medical negligence, battery, and breaches of the Missouri Merchandising Practices Act. Although the jury's compensation award exceeds $2 million, punitive damages were annulled due to distinctions concerning negligence per se claims.

stories.title: Virginia teen, 14, launches tech initiative, distributes 2,000 refurbished devices and wins Diana Award
stories.summary: At just 14 years old, Chris Qian founded ReTech for Kids, a nonprofit dedicated to bridging the technology gap for students lacking access to digital tools. By refurbishing and distributing second-hand devices, the initiative has empowered under-resourced learners. Over three years, it has engaged more than 100 volunteers and provided 2,000 devices, earning Chris both accolades and the prestigious Diana Award for his extraordinary efforts towards educational equity.

stories.title: First Successful Release: Zoo returns 62 young snakes to wild; another release planned for 2027
stories.summary: In a remarkable conservation effort, 62 San Francisco garter snakes, previously raised in a zoo, have been successfully released into their natural environment. This project stems from the need to ensure the species’ survival, as they were originally taken from the wild. Alongside this, restoration activities are being implemented to enhance their habitat.

stories.title: Punjab Congress sets up panel to vet leaders joining from other parties ahead of 2027 polls
Evening newswrap: Parl winter session likely in 1st week of Dec; India beat New Zealand by 22 runs to clinch ODI series 3-1 & more
Two killed as car fleeing police crashes into Volkswagen in UK; 4 arrested
CRPF withdraws anti-Naxal battalion from Chhattisgarh, sent to Manipur
stories.summary: In a significant move, over 1,000 CRPF personnel have been redeployed from Chhattisgarh to Manipur amid escalating security concerns. This marks the initial full withdrawal of a battalion from anti-Naxal duties since the decline of armed Maoism. Previously, stationed in Sukma, this battalion has fought against Left Wing Extremism and conducted de-mining operations.

stories.title: Conservative Majority Victory: Conservatives win 64 seats; gas expansion faces C$13.3bn deficit
stories.summary: In a significant political shift, British Columbia has ushered in a Conservative majority government after a decade dominated by the New Democratic Party. Winning 64 out of 93 seats, the Conservatives plan to place a strong emphasis on expanding liquefied natural gas production to enhance energy policy. However, they face fiscal constraints with potential deficits looming, and the new government will need to balance economic growth with public service demands.

stories.title: Scientists have drawn a treasure map of where fossils of ancient sea life are still to be found
stories.summary: In an exciting development, researchers have pinpointed potential hotspots for fossil discoveries that remain undocumented. Focusing on the Cenozoic Era, celebrated for its rich marine biodiversity, this study seeks to enhance fossil hunting by concentrating efforts on less explored territories. Additionally, revisiting collections from natural history museums could yield new insights into ancient species, reinforcing the pursuit of understanding marine life from the past.

stories.title: Farage says Britain faces 'defencelessness', singles out Russia as top threat
Congress postpones ‘Chalo Delhi’ on Constitution Day, to hold marches across states on Nov 26
‘Chats show no mention of Pulkit’: Convict’s father seeks action in Ankita Bhandari murder case
'100% pure' or just marketing? What the law says about misleading food labels
stories.summary: In India, many food products carry misleading labels, which raises serious concerns regarding consumer safety and protection. The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, addresses these issues, yet violations persist frequently. Online grocery shopping has exacerbated these discrepancies, complicating accountability for e-commerce platforms. Consumers are encouraged to document discrepancies, approach grievance officers, and report violations to relevant authorities.

stories.title: Massachusetts man, 85, loses $1M in alleged fake Brazil farmland romance scam
stories.summary: An 85-year-old man sent over $1 million to a woman claiming she needed it for taxes and legal fees. Maria Auxiliadora Rezende allegedly fabricated a story concerning inherited farmland in Brazil. Family members noticed unusual transactions and investigated the situation after voicing concerns. Authorities arrested Rezende and she faces a federal indictment for wire fraud.

stories.title: A Philadelphia wetland damaged by old dikes and dredging is being reconnected to a creek
stories.summary: Restoration efforts have begun in the Henderson Marsh area at the John Heinz National Wildlife Refuge, focusing on the excavation of channels to facilitate better water flow. This initiative not only aims to boost wildlife habitats but also enhances flood resilience for nearby communities like Eastwick. The project's success relies on collaboration among various conservation groups, along with upgraded visitor amenities to attract more nature enthusiasts to the refuge.

stories.title: Illinois family awarded $28M in birth injury lawsuit
stories.summary: Teray Boyd received a $28 million verdict following her child's traumatic birth experience, where brain damage resulted from the medical team's failure to execute an emergency C-section. The infant was delivered in dire condition, suffering from oxygen deprivation during labor. Inspired by her journey, Boyd founded two charities focused on assisting young mothers and children with disabilities, underscoring the vital importance of rigorous medical standards during childbirth.

stories.title: Ebro Ahmed Day: Ahmed stopped runaway bus; 19 schoolchildren escaped injury
stories.summary: When Ebro Ahmed spotted a school bus rolling with its door ajar and a driver incapacitated, his instincts kicked in. He quickly jumped aboard and halted the vehicle, safeguarding 19 young lives. The driver was promptly taken to the hospital and is recovering well. For his bravery, Ahmed was honored with accolades, including a dedicated day in St. Paul.

stories.title: A Berkeley scientist spent more than a decade listening to zebra finches
stories.summary: Dr. Julie Elie has meticulously created an acoustic dictionary showcasing zebra finch calls, categorizing 11 distinct vocalization types. Her groundbreaking research suggests that these birds actively comprehend the meanings of their calls, indicating that zebra finches employ a nuanced communication method. This could revolutionize human perspectives on interspecies dialogue, promoting reciprocal understanding. Nevertheless, fully unraveling avian communication remains a complex, ongoing research endeavor for many scientists.

stories.title: Redrawing Pak: Ministers back 12-province plan but pol, constitutional hurdles remain
stories.summary: Pakistan is considering expanding its administrative framework by increasing its provinces from four to twelve, aiming for more efficient governance. Senior officials argue that smaller provinces could enhance public service delivery. Yet, this ambitious initiative faces political hurdles and requires unity among major parties. Redefining boundaries will necessitate constitutional amendments, and a potential referendum may follow, pending parliamentary consent.

stories.title: Yogi targets ‘chaacha-bhatija’, says SP-era jobs came through bribes and recommendations
Iran speaker says Tehran will not accept ‘neither war nor peace’ situation, sets conditions for US deal
'Glory to Mother Chhathi!' PM Modi wishes 'renewed awareness and vitality' for all
'CBI probe into Ajit Pawar's death, name Pune Ring Road after him,' Rohit Pawar urges Amit Shah
DK Shivakumar says proposal to induct woman minister in Karnataka cabinet placed before Congress high command
Spain’s Canary Islands record highest daily migrant arrivals since 2020; 1,488 rescued
Parliament winter session likely in 1st week of December; delimitation bill to be in focus
IndiGo Guwahati-bound flight returns safely to Pune after landing gear fails to retract
stories.summary: An IndiGo Airbus A320 encountered a landing gear malfunction shortly after departing from Pune. Prioritizing safety, the flight returned to Pune International Airport. After approximately two hours of holding to deplete fuel and assess the gear, the aircraft landed without incident. To ensure minimal disruption, IndiGo arranged an alternate flight for the passengers, reinforcing the airline's commitment to their safety and comfort in challenging situations.

stories.title: 'Congress hates tribal heroes': BJP slams Rahul Gandhi for skipping Birsa Munda tribute ceremony
Major accident averted as empty Vande Bharat travels 463 km with faulty brakes
Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary greets devotees as millions prepare to observe Chhath
stories.summary: Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary extended greetings for the Sandhya Arghya as Chhath Puja commenced. Many devotees are expected to participate in offering 'arghya' to the setting sun across the state. Safety arrangements involve deploying disaster response teams and local volunteers at various ghats. The festival will conclude with prayers to the rising sun on the following day.

stories.title: 'You brought them in dumper truck': J&K BJP MLA's emotional outburst over handling of slain SPOs' bodies
stories.summary: BJP MLA Shagun Parihar criticised J&K authorities over the alleged disrespectful handling of two slain Special Police Officers' bodies, claiming they were transported in a dumper truck. She questioned the delay in addressing their families' concerns, saying officials acted only after intervention from the Lieutenant Governor. The bodies of Rashpal Kumar, 45, and Bobby Chand, 57, were recovered from Kishtwar forests on Thursday, with bullet injuries, after they went missing on November 10.

stories.title: ‘Abandoned tribals to Naxal violence’: PM Modi takes aim at previous govts
Congo Ebola outbreak claims nearly half of infected as cases cross 11,000
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in over 11,000 cases and high fatalities. Basic health measures are inadequate, with most cases detected outside surveillance systems. Children are particularly affected, contributing to rising death rates due to lack of care. Attacks on health workers and facilities have further complicated containment efforts.

stories.title: ‘Utterly ridiculous take’: US official rejects report claiming Quad is on ‘life support’ under Trump
stories.summary: The United States has dismissed a media report suggesting the Quad alliance is struggling under the Trump administration. Senior State Department official Dylan Johnson called the assessment utterly ridiculous and highlighted regular diplomatic engagements among the four countries. A potential leaders' summit in Manila is set to be formalized during upcoming ASEAN meetings.

stories.title: Chicago photographer's $220 thrift store paintings sell for $135,000 after rare discovery
stories.summary: In an unexpected twist of fate, a photographer from Chicago stumbled upon two remarkable original pieces by Warner Sallman in a thrift store back in 2016. After investing $220 for them, his diligence paid off two years later when he sold the artworks to author Jerry Jenkins for an impressive $135,000, reshaping the market landscape for Sallman’s creations and showcasing the hidden treasures often overlooked in thrift shops.

stories.title: Hungarian investigators found $19.5 million in cash buried in forests and hidden in buildings while probing allegations against a former minister
stories.summary: Hungary's anti-corruption efforts have yielded significant results, uncovering over $19.5 million in cash, stashed away in forests and hidden properties. Former minister Miklós Seszták faces bribery charges tied to the transport sector, while Prime Minister Peter Magyar's initiative seeks to address corruption issues involving the previous administration of Viktor Orbán. The Fidesz party has distanced itself from Seszták's allegations and calls for him to defend his reputation.

stories.title: IndiGo flight’s landing gear fails to retract after take-off, makes safe emergency landing in Pune
Skeletons Cheer Cancer Patient: Ohio display encouraged Tammy during treatment; figures stay out year-round
stories.summary: In Oxford, Ohio, Bill Pyle's Halloween skeleton display became a beacon of hope for Tammy during her cancer journey. After receiving a touching letter, Pyle arranged the skeletons to honor her final radiation treatment, which shifted his perspective and deepened community bonds. This display is now a year-round fixture, updated weekly, with an annual homage to Tammy, illustrating how simple decorations can uplift during tough times.

stories.title: India opposes UN call for death penalty moratorium, says no global consensus
stories.summary: India expressed its opposition to a UN resolution advocating for a global moratorium on the death penalty, reinforcing the sovereignty of individual states regarding capital punishment. By supporting lawful executions under international law, it emphasized that discussions around the death penalty were being mischaracterized in the context of extrajudicial killings.

stories.title: ‘These tricks don’t work on me’: Eisenkot rejects Netanyahu’s 'unity govt' appeal
stories.summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated his call for a national unity government. Gadi Eisenkot, his political rival, dismissed Netanyahu's appeal, viewing it as a strategy to create division. Eisenkot is currently negotiating to form his government, with a deadline of 28 days. Discussions are strained over the Knesset speaker election, with both sides presenting opposing candidates. Netanyahu's coalition proposal excludes Arab parties, complicating the negotiations ahead.

stories.title: Committed to ensure all inconsistencies in voter lists are addressed: EC to SC
Tens of thousands protest across Portugal over soaring housing costs
stories.summary: Protests occurred in over 30 cities across Portugal, reflecting increasing frustration over rising housing costs and insufficient incomes. Many protesters, including students and professionals, expressed concern about the affordability of housing. Demonstrators called for stronger tenant protections and limits on rent increases amidst growing inequality. The government promised to implement measures for affordable housing but acknowledged that changes will take time.

stories.title: Faith, pollution and politics: How Yamuna takes centre stage every Chhath Puja
US judge halts Trump's plan to close historic DC golf course for redevelopment
stories.summary: A US judge has issued a temporary block on President Trump's plan to close East Potomac Park. The ruling comes amid a legal challenge regarding the redevelopment of the historic public golf course. US District Judge Ana Reyes found that the government violated federal laws in seeking the closure. Trump plans to replace the existing courses with an 18-hole championship-level facility for major tournaments.

stories.title: UK PM Burnham's speechwriter caught using ChatGPT to draft speech
stories.summary: An anonymous speechwriter for Prime Minister Andy Burnham was seen using ChatGPT to draft a keynote address. The speech focused on criticizing former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher's legacy and addressing the cost-of-living crisis. Burnham emphasized the importance of these issues during his talk with Welsh Labour members. Opposition members have criticized both the aide's actions and Burnham’s government's plans to address economic challenges.

stories.title: Swiss men take to streets, call for stronger fight against violence against women
stories.summary: Men gathered in the Swiss capital to protest against misogyny and violence directed at women. The demonstration called for men to take an active role in opposing misogynistic views, especially online. Organizers stressed the need for men to acknowledge their responsibility in challenging these attitudes. The event followed increased awareness of violence committed by men, highlighting the importance of addressing harmful masculinity.

stories.title: Hamas confirms death of senior commander Samir Abu Younis in Israeli airstrike
stories.summary: In a recent Israeli airstrike, senior Hamas commander Samir Abu Younis was killed in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis, an incident that also left many injured. Known for his involvement in the planning of the deadly October 7 assault on Israel, his funeral is set for Sunday. The ongoing conflict continues to claim significant casualties on both sides since the ceasefire in October 2025.

stories.title: Prince William, Kate to arrive in India in first joint overseas tour since 2022
stories.summary: Kate Middleton will join Prince William in Mumbai for the 2026 Earthshot Prize awards event. This visit marks their first overseas engagement together since her cancer diagnosis in 2024. The awards will bring together notable personalities and focus on environmental challenges and innovation. Kate has been gradually returning to public life after her recovery, which has had its challenges.

stories.title: Cede Donbas to Russia to join Nato, US tells Ukraine
stories.summary: Zelensky: May Put To Vote If We Get Broad Guarantees

stories.title: Jimothy Card Auction: Rare card sells for $20,100; proceeds may fund Abby’s college
stories.summary: A young baseball enthusiast from Seattle secured an esteemed baseball card during a Mariners game. This unique card showcased Jimothy, a raccoon who captured the internet's attention due to his extraordinary look. Initially a complimentary giveaway, the card has now emerged as a remarkable collectible valued at an astonishing $20,100. With multiple offers pouring in, her family decided to auction it on eBay, generating significant buzz.

stories.title: A bronze leg found in 1820 considered Roman loot now believed to belong to a statue of Antoninus Pius
stories.summary: Emperor Antoninus Pius, celebrated for his peace-driven rule and military expeditions, may have a newly discovered connection to history. A bronze leg unearthed in Scotland suggests a statue that honored him was disassembled by Roman forces prior to their withdrawal in AD 161, challenging prior beliefs of theft. This discovery sheds light on how Rome strategically managed its monuments, and further archaeological investigations could reveal more insights.

stories.title: Australian buyer wins back $220,000 deposit in a $2.2 million land deal dispute
UK to extradite PIO bizman to US for cancer drugs fraud
Pennsylvania father barred mother from daughters' school photos and tennis matches; court upheld her authority
stories.summary: In a recent custody case between John M Surma and Julie S Surma, a Pennsylvania court affirmed that the mother retains primary authority over extracurricular activities. The evidence presented indicated that the father imposed limitations on her involvement in various school events. John Surma expressed concerns that this ruling diminished his influence on his daughters.

stories.title: A 10-year-old boy noticed his father's speech slurring during a drive; helps his dad survive a stroke
stories.summary: During a road trip to Georgia, Taylor Fritts showcased incredible presence of mind when his father suffered a stroke. While driving in Sweetwater, Tennessee, he observed his father's peculiar speech and actions. Without hesitation, Taylor contacted emergency services, leading to a swift hospital transfer via helicopter. His bravery earned him recognition as a 'Stroke Champion', highlighting the unbreakable bond between father and son.

stories.title: In 2024, New Jersey began restoring a 290-acre marsh and former industrial site
stories.summary: Cape May County has launched an ambitious restoration project aimed at revitalizing its local ecosystem. By focusing on rejuvenating tidal flow and creating new wildlife habitats, the area is already witnessing the return of various aquatic prey and bird species. The initiative also includes protective measures for freshwater ecosystems, promoting a balanced environment while enhancing public access with newly built trails and recreational facilities.

stories.title: Pak sending 'experienced' minister for Delhi event
Govt opens applications for companies to be consent managers under data law
Hospital COO accused of fake invoices and $1 million in kickbacks
Texas appeals court upholds sale of marital home despite wife's challenge to $685,000 offer
stories.summary: In a Texas court, a woman expressed her discontent with the ruling permitting a receiver to sell her marital home. The appellate court upheld the initial decision, dismissing her objections to the receiver's role in accepting a $685,000 offer for the house. The ruling clarified that her financial stake did not afford her control over the sale, highlighting the need for precise wording in divorce agreements related to property transactions.

stories.title: 2 Infants buried in Peru about 1,600 years ago; one had a rare fatal birth defect called cyclopia
stories.summary: In southern Peru, archaeologists uncovered the remains of two infants buried together, one exhibiting cyclopia. Genetic analysis confirmed that the infant with cyclopia had trisomy 13, a chromosomal condition. Their burial in a single ceramic vessel reveals insights into ancient funerary practices. Researchers highlighted that the infant's condition did not result in unusual treatment in life or death. This discovery emphasizes the historical presence of congenital differences in human populations.

stories.title: Magsaysay awardee in SC: 'Whistleblower Act in limbo for 12 yrs'
China border now 'more alive', has got infra, military boost: Jaishankar
Shah interacts with trainee IPS officers on national security, law & order
Florida court upholds removal of daughter who represented estate and trusts without a lawyer
stories.summary: In a recent ruling, Kerrin Friedman faced a significant legal setback when the Florida Third District Court of Appeal upheld her removal as personal representative of her mother’s estate and trustee of three family trusts. Her failure to comply with court mandates for legal counsel led to this decision, emphasizing her inability to manage the estate and trust affairs without proper authorization.

stories.title: Researchers track Carnaby's cockatoos in Western Australia; find native habitat helps in conservation
stories.summary: Urbanization is significantly impacting the habitats of Carnaby's cockatoos in Western Australia. Research indicates that these birds are forced to travel longer distances in search of food across divided landscapes. Even minor patches of native vegetation play a vital role as connections between larger habitats. It's essential for conservation initiatives to prioritize these smaller areas to safeguard wildlife.

stories.title: Rod Anderson spent 81 years not knowing his father till a DNA match connected him with his half-sister
stories.summary: After 81 years of searching for answers about his father, Rod Anderson finally uncovered his family's history thanks to a DNA test. His father, Charles Blakney, served in the Canadian military during World War II in England. Blakney's granddaughter, Bethany Allen, took on the mystery and connected with Anderson, highlighting how wartime bonds can profoundly influence family dynamics. This newfound connection has brought Anderson much-needed closure.

stories.title: A seven-year-old’s letter to Santa inspires charity delivering 400,000 gifts
Pitroda dismisses Rahul's claim PM tapping his phone
Democracy destroyed in '14, 'fascists' running India: Rahul
Indiana appeals court revises child support, awards father $15,275 and restores mother's obligation
stories.summary: In a recent case, a father requested modifications to his child support payments after both daughters moved in with him. This resulted in financial arguments and disputes over parenting-time credits involving their mother. stories.summary: In a pivotal ruling, a Texas appeals court declared that the Lake Bonanza Property Owners Association bears no responsibility for a brawl involving its volunteer treasurer. This incident unfolded during a budget meeting where tensions escalated, leading to a physical confrontation between treasurer Courtney and a resident after the meeting was recorded. The court determined that Courtney acted outside his official capacity, resulting in a decision favoring the homeowners association.

'Brahmins' have been consulted: Akhilesh says he will visit Ram Temple
As dal prices rise despite robust availability, govt makes weekly disclosure mandatory

Appeals court revives lawsuit by Arizona woman barred from sleeping in her car due to OCD
stories.summary: A federal appeals court has permitted Sabrina Beram to continue her disability discrimination lawsuit against the City of Sedona. Beram suffers from severe obsessive-compulsive disorder, leading her to sleep in her car due to unclean conditions in her apartment. The court ruled that she has adequately demonstrated an injury and potential future enforcement risk. Sedona's law prohibits sleeping in vehicles, even on private property, contributing to her situation.

stories.title: Florida brothers, 17 and 15, rescue mother, son and 3 dogs from floodwaters
stories.summary: In the face of severe flooding in Palm Bay, Brittany Grant and her son Nikoa found themselves trapped in their home. Seeking assistance online, their neighbor Stephanie Fanguy mobilized a rescue, with her sons, Lucas and Jonah, using a kayak and paddleboard to reach them. Remarkably, they also evacuated the family's three dogs. This incident serves as a testament to the power of community solidarity during crises.

stories.title: The Block judges list two €1 homes for €195,000, pics inside
stories.summary: Shaynna Blaze and Darren Palmer have renovated a derelict house in Castronovo di Sicilia, originally bought for €1. The fully furnished two-bedroom home features a blend of historic and contemporary design elements. It now includes a Mediterranean-style garden and a terrace bar with captivating views. The listing price is €195,000, offering buyers a chance to experience small-town Sicilian life.

stories.title: 'Visa matters are sovereign': MEA responds after 115 foreign speakers denied nod for Congress event
stories.summary: The ministry of external affairs defended its visa decisions against allegations of cancellations for the Bharat Summit. Reports indicated that over 100 foreign speakers were denied entry or had visas revoked prior to the event. Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng's visa cancellation drew significant attention due to her past interactions with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Georgia warehouses once planned for ICE detention centers now listed for sale after local opposition
stories.summary: Plans to transform warehouses in Georgia into immigration detention centres have been officially scrapped following strong backlash from local residents. Concerns raised about public safety and declining property values triggered rapid intervention from elected representatives. The General Services Administration will now proceed to auction off the previously purchased properties. Community leaders are optimistic about fostering beneficial commercial developments instead of the abandoned detention centre initiative.

Air India, Air India Express suspend flights to Riyadh, Dammam till Nov 30; Jeddah till Nov 21 amid threat
stories.summary: Air India and Air India Express have announced an extension of their flight suspensions to Riyadh and Dammam until November 30, with Jeddah flights suspended until November 21. This decision, impacting also IndiGo and Akasa Air, arises from the increased instability in the region due to threats from Yemen's Houthi militia. Affected passengers may reschedule or obtain refunds for their bookings.

Darth Vader’s lightsaber sells for a record $4.875 million
stories.summary: A lightsaber used by Darth Vader was sold for $4.875 million at the Ultimate Star Wars Auction. This sale set a new world record for any Star Wars collectible. The lightsaber surpassed previous auction records for both props and poster art. The auction featured the largest collection of Star Wars lightsabers ever offered, including twenty-seven other pieces. This reflects the increasing demand for screen-used film props among collectors.

stories.title: NY appeals court upholds father's custody after mother's addiction treatment
stories.summary: A ruling by a New York appeals court has solidified a father's primary custody of his two children, shifting them from their maternal grandparents in North Carolina back to him. The mother, battling alcoholism, attempted to regain custody but faced significant legal hurdles. The court scrutinized her sobriety and domestic violence allegations, leading to an ongoing custody dispute with more petitions yet to come.

stories.title: ICE agent who fatally shot Colombian immigrant in Maine sent racist emails about sister's Colombian partner, his mother says he should not have weapons
Times Hospitality Icons Jaipur celebrates quality and innovation in hospitality
101-year-old WWII veteran recalls how his wife helped rebuild his life after the war
stories.summary: Joseph Allegretti, a distinguished World War II veteran, reminisces about his profound journey shaped by combat and companionship. After returning from war, he embarked on a beautiful 72-year marriage with Janet Kajano, a woman who transformed his life. They raised four children together, creating a rich tapestry of community involvement and travel.

PK rules out thaw with Bihar CM, says meeting won't turn 'class 7-fail into PhD holder'
IAF 'honeytrap' case: Wing Commander leaked war plans to Pakistan spy for nudes
Texas couple find strangers building on their land after alleged identity fraud; court dismisses notary claims
stories.summary: A couple in Texas discovered their property had been allegedly sold by an impersonator. After construction began on the land, they informed the parties involved of the dispute. The notary claimed he was not responsible as the notarization occurred in Colorado. The Texas Fourth Court of Appeals ruled there was no personal jurisdiction over the notary. This case highlights issues of jurisdiction in property transactions when services cross state lines.

6 dead after building collapses near Kenya's capital
New Jersey man faces $91,500 penalty over refusal to grant religious divorce
stories.summary: A federal appeals court has revived parts of a New Jersey man's lawsuit against his former wife over a religious divorce dispute. The case involves a $91,500 penalty imposed after he failed to provide a Jewish religious divorce document. The court has asked a lower court to examine his claims separately.

Pakistani beauty cream seized in Maharashtra found with mercury 48,000 times over limit
stories.summary: Maharashtra authorities have taken action by seizing beauty creams in Nanded that contained alarmingly high levels of mercury, valued at Rs 40 lakh. Laboratory analysis revealed that these creams posed severe health risks due to toxic contents beyond acceptable limits. Officials have issued a public alert against usage, and a legal case under drug safety regulations has been filed.

Manipur 2023 violence probe commission gets 7th extension, report due by May 20, 2027
stories.summary: The investigation into the ethnic violence in Manipur has received an extension until May 20, 2027. This unrest, which began on May 3, 2023, led to more than 300 fatalities and left thousands displaced. The commission will delve into the origins, escalation, and governmental responses to the turmoil. Initially scheduled to wrap up by November 2023, the inquiry has been extended multiple times to ensure a thorough examination of evidence.

Drunk raccoon helps raise $290,000 for Virginia animal shelter
stories.summary: In a hilarious turn of events, a raccoon broke into a Virginia liquor store last November, delighted in a drinking spree, and ended up napping in the bathroom. This escapade quickly became an internet hit, prompting the creation of themed merchandise that raised over $290,000 for the Hanover County shelter. The 'Trashed Panda' has become a mascot of support for the shelter's growth efforts.

stories.title: 'No NCP merger talks': Maharashtra minister Bharne after meeting Sunetra Pawar
Court upholds contractual payments: ex-husband must keep paying fuel, health cover
stories.summary: A Louisiana appeals court has upheld a legal agreement requiring a divorced husband to keep paying his ex-wife's expenses. The court ruled these payments represent contractual duties rather than typical spousal support subject to change upon remarriage. Previous agreements concerning property and payments have been recognized, and the validity of the house deed has been affirmed. Both parties will bear the appeal costs, and either party can seek a rehearing.

stories.title: New York man gets up to 21 years for stealing $4.7 million Harlem homes
stories.summary: Joseph Makhani has been sentenced to seven to 21 years in prison for using forged documents to steal two Harlem brownstones worth $4.7 million. His scheme left an elderly homeowner living in a homeless shelter while he collected more than $12,000 in monthly rent from one of the properties.

stories.title: Indiana court backs daughter as sole representative of father's estate after family dispute
stories.summary: An Indiana appeals court has upheld the removal of Rebecca Johnson as co-administrator of Shane Fields' estate after disputes over estate management and legal representation. Fields died in a 2025 Kentucky road accident, leaving a wife and five children. The court found that Johnson's refusal to follow court orders and cooperate with the other representative delayed the estate's legal claims. His daughter, Hailey Daniels, will remain the sole administrator.

stories.title: Massachusetts woman grows mushrooms in basement, builds 1,000-pound weekly farm
'My phone tapped': Rahul fires salvo at PM Modi; 'get head examined', says BJP
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi accused PM Narendra Modi of having his phone tapped and renewed his challenge for a face-to-face debate. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav backed his allegation, saying technology could not be trusted in the age of AI. The BJP rejected the charge, with Kerala BJP chief Rajeev Chandrasekhar hitting back at the Congress leader.

stories.title: 'Hopeful they will come': India on inviting Pakistan to SCO Civilisational Forum in Delhi
stories.summary: India has invited Pakistan to participate in the inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. This event is scheduled to take place from November 20 to 22, featuring various participating countries. Union culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat expressed hope that Pakistan would attend the forum. The discussions will focus on cultural ties and shared civilisational heritage among member states.

'India showed world yoga': PM Modi praises HV Sheshadri at Bengaluru event
'No long speeches': Rahul Gandhi renews debate challenge to PM Modi with a 'guarantee'
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has renewed his challenge for a public debate with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during an Instagram session. He claimed he was unable to speak freely in Parliament and called for direct allegations against each other. Gandhi suggested a debate moderated by a neutral party, including options like RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat. BJP leaders dismissed his calls, emphasizing that Parliament serves as an appropriate platform for discussions.
